description: [phase 3.8 38j, kind `input`] loadFlic 0x0043d740 calls pumpInput483bd0 at +0x54 on every load (114 to 120 loads per loadWorldAssets for the course types 0..3, 29 for any other value) and the drawing between loads reads jgld's Palette::update QPC; a message dispatched by one of those pumps would follow a palette QPC clock record, so tick.cpp parse_trace classifies its batch as a frame-body batch, and the port's loadFlic (module menu) takes no dispatch there. In every run of this stream (the 4 title-menu segments, the cov_b_shots / cov_b_shots2 / cov_k1_animals / cov_b_career_types chains) every dispatch was delivered and none was left, so no recorded input arrives during a world load in the corpus.
path to resolution: If a recording has a dispatch inside a world load: give TraceInput the loadFlic pump site (a pump_at site) and accept a body-classified batch there.

description: [phase 3.8 38j, kind `input`] In a modal loop (the title menu's hover loop 0x00421025, the browsers, the difficulty and location screens) the original reads the cursor once more for each WM_MOUSEMOVE it dispatches (a CURSOR record between the MSG 512 record and the next handler record; e.g. cov_b_career_types/00 trace positions 4094, 7732, 8136), a read the port's pumps do not make. TraceInput then delivers that dispatch at the first pump call whose cursor reads reach the batch's count (the loops read one cursor per pass, so one pass later); the cursor position is the same then. Measured: 2 cursor reads under in each of the 4 title-menu segments, all dispatches delivered, 0 at another cursor count, PASS. Which jgld routine makes the read is not determined.
path to resolution: Locate the read in jgld.dll's message handling and let the port's pump make it, if a recording ever needs the exact read count.
